docs.title: Keyso Language
docs.text:
Keyso is a dictionary-based language for describing finite sets of configurations.

A Keyso document does not describe one configuration only. It describes a configuration space: a finite set whose elements are configurations.

{
  "_product": [
    {"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]},
    {"optimization": ["O0", "O2"]}
  ]
}

This describes the four configurations obtained by combining the two compiler choices with the two optimization choices.

docs.title: Scope of this documentation
docs.text:
This website documents the Keyso language only.

It intentionally does not document any parser, emitter, package, command-line tool, or implementation API. A Keyso document may be represented by any host system that can represent dictionaries, lists, strings, numbers, booleans, and null-like values.

docs.title: Core ideas
docs.text:
• A configuration is a mapping from keys to values.
  • A configuration type is the set of keys present in a configuration.
  • A configuration space is a finite set of configurations with the same type.
  • _product combines independent configuration spaces with disjoint keys.
  • _union, _intersection, and _difference operate on configuration spaces with the same type.
  • _set explicitly enumerates a finite configuration space.
  • _literal marks an object as data.
  • _nested evaluates an independent Keyso document and uses each result as a value.

docs.title: Minimal example
docs.text:
{
  "_product": [
    {"system": ["jedi", "jupiter"]},
    {"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]},
    {"mpi": ["openmpi", "mpich"]}
  ]
}

The result is a configuration space with type:

{system, compiler, mpi}

docs.title: Language Overview
docs.text:
Keyso is a small dictionary language for describing configuration spaces by combining simple constructs with set operations.

The language is deliberately based on a data model rather than a text format. Examples in this documentation use dictionary notation, but the semantics are independent of whether a document is written, stored, or transmitted using a particular serialization.

docs.title: Constructs
docs.text:
Keyso has two kinds of constructs:

  1. Value constructs, used as values of ordinary keys.
  2. Space constructs, used to construct configuration spaces.

Value constructs:

Construct Meaning ordinary scalar one possible value list multiple possible values for one key _literal treat the contained object as data _nested evaluate an independent Keyso document and use its results as values

Space constructs:

Construct Meaning key-value mapping one configuration with one key key-multivalue mapping one key with several possible values _set explicit finite set of configurations _product product of spaces with disjoint types _union union of spaces with the same type _intersection intersection of spaces with the same type _difference difference of two spaces with the same type

docs.title: Explicit product rule
docs.text:
A dictionary with several ordinary keys is not a shorthand for product.

This is invalid:

{
  "compiler": ["gcc", "clang"],
  "optimization": ["O0", "O2"]
}

Use _product instead:

{
  "_product": [
    {"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]},
    {"optimization": ["O0", "O2"]}
  ]
}

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
A configuration is a finite mapping from keys to values.

{
  "compiler": "gcc",
  "optimization": "O2"
}

This concrete configuration contains two key-value pairs.

docs.title: Configuration type
docs.text:
The type of a configuration is the set of keys present in the configuration.

For this configuration:

{
  "compiler": "gcc",
  "optimization": "O2"
}

The type is:

{compiler, optimization}

docs.title: Configuration space
docs.text:
A configuration space is a finite set of configurations with the same type.

{
  "_set": [
    {"compiler": "gcc", "optimization": "O2"},
    {"compiler": "clang", "optimization": "O3"}
  ]
}

Both configurations have the same type:

{compiler, optimization}

docs.title: Coherence of types
docs.text:
Two configuration spaces have coherent types when their types are equal.

Coherent spaces may be combined using:

  • _union
  • _intersection
  • _difference

Two configuration spaces have anticoherent types when their types are disjoint.

Anticoherent spaces may be combined using:

  • _product

docs.title: Homogeneity
docs.text:
Every configuration space has exactly one type.

This is invalid because the two configurations do not have the same keys:

{
  "_set": [
    {"compiler": "gcc"},
    {"compiler": "clang", "optimization": "O2"}
  ]
}

docs.title: Compiler matrix
docs.text:
{
  "_product": [
    {"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]},
    {"optimization": ["O0", "O2", "O3"]}
  ]
}

docs.title: HPC run matrix
docs.text:
{
  "_product": [
    {"system": ["jedi", "jupiter"]},
    {"nodes": [1, 2, 4]},
    {"tasks_per_node": [4, 8]}
  ]
}

docs.title: Explicit exceptional cases
docs.text:
{
  "_set": [
    {"compiler": "gcc", "optimization": "O2"},
    {"compiler": "clang", "optimization": "O3"}
  ]
}

docs.title: Add one special case to a product
docs.text:
{
  "_union": [
    {
      "_product": [
        {"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]},
        {"optimization": ["O2", "O3"]}
      ]
    },
    {
      "_set": [
        {"compiler": "intel", "optimization": "O2"}
      ]
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Remove an unsupported combination
docs.text:
{
  "_difference": {
    "_minuend": {
      "_product": [
        {"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]},
        {"optimization": ["O0", "O2"]}
      ]
    },
    "_subtrahend": {
      "_set": [
        {"compiler": "clang", "optimization": "O0"}
      ]
    }
  }
}

docs.title: Nested build and run sections
docs.text:
{
  "_product": [
    {"system": ["jedi", "jupiter"]},
    {
      "build": {
        "_nested": {
          "_product": [
            {"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]},
            {"mpi": ["openmpi", "mpich"]}
          ]
        }
      }
    },
    {
      "run": {
        "_nested": {
          "_product": [
            {"nodes": [1, 2]},
            {"tasks_per_node": [4, 8]}
          ]
        }
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Literals and Nesting
docs.text:
Dictionaries can appear in two different roles:

  1. as Keyso documents that should be interpreted, or
  2. as data values that should be preserved.

To avoid ambiguity, Keyso requires explicit markers for dictionary values.

docs.title: Literal values
docs.text:
Use _literal when a dictionary is ordinary data.

{
  "params": {
    "_literal": {
      "nx": 128,
      "ny": 128,
      "solver": ["cg", "gmres"]
    }
  }
}

Result:

[
  {
    "params": {
      "nx": 128,
      "ny": 128,
      "solver": ["cg", "gmres"]
    }
  }
]

The contents of _literal are not interpreted as Keyso.

docs.title: Nested Keyso documents
docs.text:
Use _nested when the value of a key should be produced by an independent Keyso document.

{
  "build": {
    "_nested": {
      "_product": [
        {"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]},
        {"optimization": ["O2", "O3"]}
      ]
    }
  }
}

Result:

[
  {"build": {"compiler": "gcc", "optimization": "O2"}},
  {"build": {"compiler": "gcc", "optimization": "O3"}},
  {"build": {"compiler": "clang", "optimization": "O2"}},
  {"build": {"compiler": "clang", "optimization": "O3"}}
]

The inner keys are not part of the outer type. The outer type is:

{build}

docs.title: Plain dictionary values are invalid
docs.text:
This is invalid because it is ambiguous:

{
  "params": {
    "nx": 128,
    "ny": 128
  }
}

Use _literal for data or _nested for an independently evaluated Keyso document.

docs.title: Normal Form
docs.text:
Every finite Keyso document can be represented as an explicit _set.

For example:

{
  "_product": [
    {"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]},
    {"optimization": ["O0", "O2"]}
  ]
}

has the normal form:

{
  "_set": [
    {"compiler": "gcc", "optimization": "O0"},
    {"compiler": "gcc", "optimization": "O2"},
    {"compiler": "clang", "optimization": "O0"},
    {"compiler": "clang", "optimization": "O2"}
  ]
}

Normal form is useful for:

  • comparing two Keyso documents,
  • inspecting the exact generated configuration space,
  • removing duplicate configurations,
  • serializing the final result of set operations.

docs.title: Empty spaces
docs.text:
A set operation may produce an empty configuration space.

{
  "_difference": {
    "_minuend": {"compiler": ["gcc"]},
    "_subtrahend": {"compiler": ["gcc"]}
  }
}

The result has no configurations, but it still has a type:

{compiler}

This matters because empty spaces can still participate in later set operations as typed spaces.

docs.title: Reserved keywords
docs.text: Keyword Role _literal Treat the contained object as a value _nested Evaluate the contained Keyso document independently and use its results as values _set Explicitly enumerate a finite configuration space _product Product of spaces with disjoint types _union Union of spaces with equal types _intersection Intersection of spaces with equal types _difference Difference of two spaces with equal types _minuend Left operand of _difference _subtrahend Right operand of _difference

docs.title: Key-value
docs.text: {"key": "value"}

docs.title: Key-multivalue
docs.text: {"key": ["value1", "value2"]}

docs.title: Explicit set
docs.text:
{
  "_set": [
    {"key1": "value1", "key2": "value2"},
    {"key1": "value3", "key2": "value4"}
  ]
}

docs.title: Product
docs.text:
{
  "_product": [
    {"key1": ["a", "b"]},
    {"key2": ["c", "d"]}
  ]
}

docs.title: Union
docs.text:
{
  "_union": [
    {"key": ["a", "b"]},
    {"key": ["b", "c"]}
  ]
}

docs.title: Intersection
docs.text:
{
  "_intersection": [
    {"key": ["a", "b"]},
    {"key": ["b", "c"]}
  ]
}

docs.title: Difference
docs.text:
{
  "_difference": {
    "_minuend": {"key": ["a", "b", "c"]},
    "_subtrahend": {"key": ["b"]}
  }
}

docs.title: Type requirements
docs.text: Operation Type requirement _product operands must have disjoint types _union operands must have equal types _intersection operands must have equal types _difference minuend and subtrahend must have equal types _set all listed configurations must have equal types

docs.title: Dictionary value rules
docs.text: Form Meaning {"key": {"_literal": object}} object is data {"key": {"_nested": keyso_document}} keyso_document is evaluated independently {"key": { ... }} invalid unless wrapped in _literal or _nested

docs.title: Set Operations
docs.text: Keyso provides set operations over configuration spaces.

docs.title: Product
docs.text:
_product combines configuration spaces with disjoint types.

{
  "_product": [
    {"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]},
    {"optimization": ["O0", "O2"]}
  ]
}

Result:

[
  {"compiler": "gcc", "optimization": "O0"},
  {"compiler": "gcc", "optimization": "O2"},
  {"compiler": "clang", "optimization": "O0"},
  {"compiler": "clang", "optimization": "O2"}
]

The operands must have disjoint types. This is invalid because both operands contain compiler:

{
  "_product": [
    {"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]},
    {"compiler": ["gcc", "intel"]}
  ]
}

docs.title: Union
docs.text:
_union combines configuration spaces with the same type.

{
  "_union": [
    {"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]},
    {"compiler": ["clang", "intel"]}
  ]
}

Result:

[
  {"compiler": "gcc"},
  {"compiler": "clang"},
  {"compiler": "intel"}
]

docs.title: Intersection
docs.text:
_intersection keeps configurations that are present in all operands.

{
  "_intersection": [
    {"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]},
    {"compiler": ["clang", "intel"]}
  ]
}

Result:

[
  {"compiler": "clang"}
]

docs.title: Difference
docs.text:
_difference removes the subtrahend space from the minuend space.

{
  "_difference": {
    "_minuend": {"compiler": ["gcc", "clang", "intel"]},
    "_subtrahend": {"compiler": ["clang"]}
  }
}

Result:

[
  {"compiler": "gcc"},
  {"compiler": "intel"}
]

docs.title: Syntax
docs.text: A Keyso document is a dictionary. A dictionary at a space position must contain exactly one construct.

docs.title: Keywords
docs.text:
The following keys are reserved:

_literal
_nested
_set
_product
_union
_intersection
_difference
_minuend
_subtrahend

Reserved keywords cannot be used as ordinary configuration keys.

docs.title: Key-value mapping
docs.text:
A single ordinary key with a single value describes a configuration space containing one configuration.

{"compiler": "gcc"}

Result:

[
  {"compiler": "gcc"}
]

docs.title: Key-multivalue mapping
docs.text:
A single ordinary key with a list value describes one configuration for each value.

{"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]}

Result:

[
  {"compiler": "gcc"},
  {"compiler": "clang"}
]

docs.title: Explicit set
docs.text:
_set explicitly enumerates a finite configuration space.

{
  "_set": [
    {"compiler": "gcc", "optimization": "O2"},
    {"compiler": "clang", "optimization": "O3"}
  ]
}

The value of _set is written as a list because that is the ordinary way to serialize a collection of dictionaries. Semantically, it is a set: duplicate configurations are ignored.

docs.title: Single construct rule
docs.text:
A space-position dictionary must contain one construct only.

Valid:

{"compiler": ["gcc", "clang"]}

Valid:

{"_product": [{"compiler": "gcc"}, {"optimization": "O2"}]}

Invalid:

{
  "compiler": ["gcc", "clang"],
  "optimization": ["O0", "O2"]
}
